correctness.rationale: For all n>=5, published Chari–Joswig Thm4.1 gives underlying wedge S²∨2S^{n-2}. The proof itself constructs boundaries of alternating incidence n-vertex sets E/O; all facets in their supports are disjoint with coefficients ±1, so these two cycles form a primitive integer top homology basis, and rotation shifts E/O as n-cycle with sign (-1)^(n-1). Reflection exchanges these two cycles up to adjustable sign. On nontrivial generator rotation there are no fixed nonempty simplices, giving reduced Lefschetz -1; top trace -2(-1)^(n-2)=-2 in alternating Euler sum, so H2 trace +1. For reflection, the invariant edge-pairs Q_j allow pure-face fixed strata of precisely two contractible simplices, each of positive size for n>=5, yielding reduced Lefschetz +1. Top trace0 forces H2 reflection sign +1. Since r,s generate D_n, H2 is trivially acted on. Independently enumerated all pure facets and fixed traces for n=5..9, with n² facets; these finite tests corroborate but do not prove all-n lemma.

value.rationale: The pure discrete-Morse complex of a cycle has a classical nonequivariant wedge decomposition; the exact integral dihedral action on the free homology lattices is a natural finer invariant. Reflection and parity-dependent rotation signs alter rational quotient Betti degrees, information invisible in ordinary homology ranks. This is a motivated structural symmetry refinement rather than a rebranding of the wedge theorem.
